channel.description: Latest articles from The Christian Post (christianpost.com)

item.title: Minn. community mourns beloved pastor, chaplain who died after helping motorist stuck in snow
item.description: A Minnesota pastor and longtime chaplain collapsed and died after helping a stranded motorist outside his church. The death of James “Jim” Bzoskie, 76, has prompted an outpouring of grief from community members and law enforcement officials. #Minnesota #PastorJamesJimBzoskie #HeartAttack #CornerstoneBibleChurch

item.title: ‘Concerning’: US gov’t speaks out after Christian woman prosecuted in UK for silently praying
item.description: A British woman has been charged under a new U.K. law for silently praying outside an abortion clinic, prompting the United States government to call the case “concerning” and a threat to religious liberty. #IsabelVaughanSpruce #prayer #abortion #bufferzones

item.title: Amy Coney Barrett warns of attacks on free speech in UK, discusses Dobbs decision
item.description: U.S. Supreme Court Associate Justice Amy Coney Barrett and Bishop Robert Barron recently discussed the similarity between liberal textual interpretations of the Bible and the U.S. Constitution during an episode of Barron's podcast that aired earlier this week. #AmyConeyBarrett #RobertBarron #SupremeCourt #AntoninScalia

item.title: Over 330,000 people sign petition opposing Macron's '21st century mark' on Notre-Dame
item.description: Over 330,000 people have signed a petition opposing new stained-glass window designs for Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris. #NotreDame #EmmanuelMacron #stainedglasswindow

item.title: Trump's week in review: Targeting ISIS in Nigeria, $3K to illegal immigrants who self-deport
item.description: Even as the Christmas holiday shortened the workweek for most Americans, multiple developments unfolded in the Trump administration this week. The administration unveiled a limited-time $3,000 incentive for illegal immigrants to self-deport before the end of the year, and the administration took military action against ISIS militants in Nigeria. #ISIS #Nigeria #Trump #Illegalimmigration

item.title: The Christian Post's top 10 news stories of 2025 (part 2)
item.description: This year, Americans witnessed numerous tragedies, including the political assassination of conservative Christian activist Charlie Kirk, but also saw signs of hope, such as the Trump administration's brokering of several peace deals worldwide. A global spotlight was placed on the persecution of Christians, particularly in Nigeria, and after years of prayer, the U.S. is finally witnessing the beginnings of the dismantling of transgender ideology. Here are CP's top stories of 2025. #ArtificialInt

item.title: Ghana’s Komba people receive complete Bible that could help preserve language from extinction
item.description: Ghana's Komba people received their complete Bible after 16 years of dedicated translation work. Translators hope the translation will deepen faith while serving as a major repository to preserve the Komba language and culture from extinction. #Ghana #Bibletranslation #Konkomba

item.title: This week in Christian history: ‘Amazing Grace’ first sung, Robert Boyle's thunderstorm conversion experience
item.description: Events that happened this week in Christian history include the first performance of “Amazing Grace,” Robert Boyle’s conversion experience and John Wycliffe suffering a stroke. #AmazingGrace #NewYearsDay #RobertBoyle #Wycliffe #history

item.title: 10 notable Christian leaders, influencers who died in 2025
item.description: In a year marked by Donald Trump's return to the White House, peace efforts in the Middle East and Eastern Europe and economic uncertainty, the world also mourned the loss of several notable Christian leaders and public figures in 2025. #PopeFrancis #JamesDobson #VoddieBaucham #KayArthur #JimmySwaggart #JohnMacArthur

item.title: ‘Treated as a criminal’: Grandmother criminally charged for inviting people to chat outside hospital
item.description: A 75-year-old woman has been criminally charged in Glasgow for standing near a hospital with a sign inviting people to chat. She is accused of violating Scotland’s buffer zone law, which prohibits influencing behavior near abortion facilities. #Scotland #UnitedKingdom #BufferZone #AbortionClinics #Prayer #Chat #FreeSpeech #Glasgow
